Which is the Killer, Current or Voltage?
As an electrical engineering technician who works on generators all day, I can tell you the answer. It's actually amperage that kills you. It takes less than 1 amp to stop your heart.
Isn't it also interesting that 60 cycles a second is the exact freq in which the human heart defibrillates?
And a typical generator runs at either 50 or 60htz. Ironic, isn't it?
Right!? This is why you see less fatalities in europe w their AC running at 50htz

Current kills.
It's not dependent on the voltage, but on the forced current that will flow through you.
Actually the amount of current that kills you is the stupidly low of 0.1-0.2 Amperes.

All voltages can be lethal.
Let's say there's an exposed cabling that powers your 30 Watt desk lamp at 110 Volts.
With some quick calculations there's aproximately 30/110 = 0.27 Amps flowing through that cable.
Now if you touch the exposed part with your finger, you will feel great pain and your finger tip will probably melt.

Let's say the same cable is still exposed but now the circuit is broken at that very part.
You have a great idea! Why not join that part with my bare hands?
So you proceed and join the two parts of the cable.
But little did you know, that upon grabing both ends, the current was forced to travel through you, from one end to another.
And that's how you passed away, with such silly last words.

Always remember guys! Better safe than sorry!
